title: 🚀 AI career
goal: First role in AI governance or AI evaluation, then on to the ethics & psychology side
notes: About 10.5 h a week. Course reading and sessions on weekday evenings; portfolio project work in longer blocks, best in the morning after the workout (deep work); writing (the learning log) about 20 min a day; networking an evening event every fortnight; from month 4, a fixed weekly applications slot. On a short (work) day, keep it light: reading, the learning log or a LinkedIn message.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.goal: Learn the field's language and get into a structured course, so you can talk credibly and add real lines to your CV.
phases.checkpoint: course started, one tiny eval run, one post published

steps.title: Apply for BlueDot Impact's AGI Strategy course
steps.details: The entry course and the gateway to their Frontier AI Governance course. Free; apply now even if the next start is weeks away.

steps.title: Rewrite your LinkedIn headline: "Technical analyst moving into AI governance & safety | Python | LLM evaluation"
Set up a GitHub repo ai-safety-portfolio and a Substack or LinkedIn newsletter
Start a learning log: one paragraph a day on what you read
steps.details: It becomes your writing material. The daily habit "AI career: learning log" keeps it going.

steps.title: Read a plain-English summary of the EU AI Act
steps.details: Risk tiers, what "high-risk" means (recruitment is one), and the obligations.

steps.title: Read the NIST AI Risk Management Framework overview
steps.details: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage.

steps.title: Read the UK's approach to AI regulation and what the UK AI Security Institute does
Check your eligibility for BPSS/SC security clearance
steps.details: UK AI Security Institute roles need it; check early given the AWS vetting issue.

steps.title: Take the free University of Helsinki "Ethics of AI" online course
steps.details: A few hours a week; can run past week 3.

steps.title: Read up on automation bias, anthropomorphism, trust calibration, persuasion and manipulation, and sycophancy in LLMs
Read one AI lab's model guidelines (Anthropic's constitution or OpenAI's model spec)
steps.details: Note what they say about honesty and user wellbeing.

steps.title: Work through the Inspect tutorial (the UK AI Security Institute's eval framework, Python)
Run one tiny eval on a model via API
steps.details: For example 20 questions with and without user pushback.

steps.title: Write and publish your first post: "What I learned in my first month studying AI governance"

phases.title: Portfolio
phases.goal: Three public pieces of work that prove you can do the job; each fills a placeholder on your CV. About 10–12 hours a week.
phases.checkpoint: Project 1 published, Project 2 drafted, CV placeholders replaced with real content

stages.title: Project 1 — LLM sycophancy and bias evaluation (weeks 5–8)

steps.title: Pick 2–3 models you can access via API
steps.details: Budget around £20–40 in credits.

steps.title: Build the sycophancy prompt set (~50)
steps.details: Factual questions, then the "user" pushes back ("I'm pretty sure that's wrong"). Measure how often a correct answer flips.

steps.title: Build the bias prompt set (~50)
steps.details: Identical CVs with only the name changed; the model rates the candidates. Measure differences in scores.

steps.title: Run them with Inspect or a Python script; save the results as CSV
Chart the results and write the README
steps.details: Method, results, limitations, and what you'd do next.

steps.title: Publish on GitHub with a 600–900 word write-up

stages.title: Project 2 — AI risk assessment of a real product (weeks 9–10)

steps.title: Pick a public AI hiring or HR tool (CV screening, video interview scoring)
Classify it under the EU AI Act and map its risks with the NIST AI RMF
steps.details: Public information only: fairness, transparency, human oversight, data protection.

steps.title: Write a 3–4 page assessment with a risk table and recommended mitigations
steps.details: Like a consultant would.

steps.title: Publish it as a PDF on your portfolio
Replace the CV placeholders with Projects 1 and 2
Read 4–6 real papers or summaries on why people over-trust chatbots
steps.details: Topic idea: "Why people over-trust chatbots: automation bias, anthropomorphism, and what designers should do". Cite them properly.

steps.title: Write the essay: 1,200–1,500 words, ending with practical recommendations
Publish on Substack or LinkedIn and share it in AI safety communities

phases.title: Network and visibility
phases.goal: Be known to 20–30 people in London's AI safety and governance scene. Many roles here fill through referrals and fellowships, not job boards.
phases.checkpoint: at least one person has referred you, or invited you to apply for something

steps.title: Join the BlueDot alumni community and AI safety Slack/Discord groups; post your projects there
Apply for BlueDot's Frontier AI Governance course
steps.details: Aimed at technical people considering governance work. Months 2–4; needs the AGI Strategy course first.

steps.title: Look into LISA (London Initiative for Safe AI) visiting/affiliate membership and events
Book 1–2 London events a month
steps.details: AI safety and governance meetups, Ada Lovelace Institute and Alan Turing Institute public events, LISA events if open.

steps.title: Find one mentor 2–5 years ahead in AI governance or evaluation
steps.details: Offer to help with a small task in return.

steps.title: Volunteer or contribute: an open-source eval repo, a research project needing a Python person, or an AI policy group
Post your learning log publicly once a month

phases.title: Applying and interviewing
phases.goal: Land your first role in governance, evaluation or trust & safety. Expect 40–80 applications; quality matters more than volume.
phases.checkpoint: an offer in governance, evaluation or trust & safety, or a fellowship place

steps.title: Set up the applications tracker: role, date, contact, stage, outcome
steps.details: Review weekly what's getting replies.

steps.title: Make a target list of employers
steps.details: UK AI Security Institute (Societal Impacts team; needs BPSS/SC), Ada Lovelace Institute, Alan Turing Institute, Google DeepMind / Anthropic / OpenAI London, Apollo Research and other eval startups, Big 4 AI assurance and risk teams, Faculty, tech trust & safety teams. Check each one's current vacancies.

steps.title: Tailor a CV profile and cover-letter base that leads with your best project
steps.details: Every application: match the profile to the job, lead with the most relevant project, and name one specific thing about the organisation's AI work.

steps.title: Apply for fellowships and programmes that take career changers
steps.details: Often the best door in.

steps.title: Apply for the Vista Institute for AI Policy course
steps.details: Legal and policy-focused; recommended after BlueDot. Months 4–8.

steps.title: Interview prep: know the EU AI Act risk tiers, the NIST AI RMF and one recent AI safety story well
Interview prep: walk through Project 1 in 3 minutes (question, method, result, limitation)
Interview prep: practise the case "How would you assess the risks of deploying a chatbot for mental health support?"
Interview prep: practise your one-line AWS answer
steps.details: "The role ended after security vetting on the project didn't progress; it showed me I want to work on the risk and impact side of technology."

phases.title: Deepen into ethics and psychology
phases.goal: Once you're inside the field, move toward the human and ethical side you care most about. A mainly ethics or psychology role at 2–4 years.
phases.checkpoint: a role that is mainly ethics or psychology

steps.title: Pick your long-term lane by month 12: human-AI interaction research, AI ethics/policy research, or model behaviour
steps.details: Your first job will show you what you enjoy. By Oct 2027.

steps.title: Choose a credential for the lane: IAPP AIGP (governance) or a part-time MSc (research)
steps.details: AIGP: self-study over a few months, exam about $799, ideally employer-funded. MSc: AI ethics, AI and society, cognitive science or a psychology conversion, part-time in London.

steps.title: Publish more seriously: a longer evaluation study, a co-authored paper, or a workshop submission
Move internally toward roles on user behaviour and wellbeing
steps.details: Trust & safety policy, user research on AI products, model behaviour teams.

habits.title: AI career: learning log (one paragraph on what you read)
habits.details: About 20 min. It becomes material for your posts.

habits.title: AI career: message someone on LinkedIn in a role you want
habits.details: Ask one specific question about their path; don't ask for a job. Two a week.

habits.title: AI career: comment thoughtfully on an AI governance post
AI career: weekly applications (2–3 stretch, 5–8 realistic, 2–3 bridge)
habits.details: About 3–4 h. Tailor each one, log it in the tracker, and check what's getting replies.
